title: Normalized inverse image of represented diagrams on subcanonical sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Assume each has finite limits and is subcanonical, meaning every presheaf $h_V=\operatorname{Hom}(-,V)$ is a sheaf of sets. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits and coverings, and let $L\dashv u^s$ be its geometric inverse-image adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], where $(u^sF)(V)=F(uV)$. For $V\in\mathcal C$ define $\beta_V:h_V\to u^sh_{uV}$ by $\beta_V(W)(a)=u(a)$, and let $c_V:Lh_V\to h_{uV}$ be its adjunct. Then $c_V$ is an isomorphism, natural in every arrow $a:V\to V'$:
$$c_{V'}\circ L(h_a)=h_{u(a)}\circ c_V.$$
For every finite diagram $V_j$ of objects of $\mathcal C$, these comparisons identify its image under $Lh$ with the diagram $h_{uV_j}$ and identify its finite-limit cones under the canonical finite-limit comparisons. In particular, if an object $G$ has multiplication $G\times G\to G$, unit $1\to G$ and inverse $G\to G$ satisfying the group identities, $c_G$ is an isomorphism of the resulting group sheaves, compatible with all homomorphisms between such represented group objects. The adjunct of $c_V$, evaluated at $\mathrm{id}_V$, is $\mathrm{id}_{uV}$.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf; normalized diagram and finite-limit compatibility are the expanded adjunction/Yoneda argument, written in report.md under Proof in words.

proof.text:
Because the sites are subcanonical, $h_V,h_{uV}$ are sheaves. The sheaf categories are full subcategories of presheaves, so Yoneda evaluation applies to their morphisms. For every sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal D$, the adjunction and Yoneda give bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Lh_V,F)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,u^sF)\simeq F(uV)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(h_{uV},F).$$
Let $\Psi_F$ denote their composite. For $r:h_{uV}\to F$, the adjunct of $r\circ c_V$ is $u^s(r)\circ\beta_V$ by naturality of the adjunction. Its value at $\mathrm{id}_V$ is $r_{uV}(u(\mathrm{id}_V))=r_{uV}(\mathrm{id}_{uV})$. The two Yoneda evaluations therefore give $\Psi_F(r\circ c_V)=r$. Since $\Psi_F$ is bijective, precomposition by $c_V$ is bijective for every $F$.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf; expanded normalized adjunction/Yoneda argument (Categories Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Take $F=Lh_V$ in the preceding precomposition bijection. There is $t:h_{uV}\to Lh_V$ with $t\circ c_V=\mathrm{id}_{Lh_V}$. For $F=h_{uV}$, the morphisms $c_V\circ t$ and $\mathrm{id}_{h_{uV}}$ have equal precomposites with $c_V$, since $(c_V\circ t)\circ c_V=c_V$. Injectivity gives $c_V\circ t=\mathrm{id}_{h_{uV}}$, proving that $c_V$ is an isomorphism. Its adjunct is the specified $\beta_V$, and $\beta_V(V)(\mathrm{id}_V)=u(\mathrm{id}_V)=\mathrm{id}_{uV}$, proving the required normalization.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf; expanded normalized adjunction/Yoneda argument (Categories Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: For $a:V\to V'$, the adjunct of $c_{V'}\circ L(h_a)$ is $\beta_{V'}\circ h_a$, whereas the adjunct of $h_{u(a)}\circ c_V$ is $u^s(h_{u(a)})\circ\beta_V$. At $W\in\mathcal C$ and $b:W\to V$, these send $b$ respectively to $u(a\circ b)$ and $u(a)\circ u(b)$, equal by functoriality. Thus the adjuncts and hence the original maps agree. This gives the stated naturality equation, and applying it to each arrow identifies every represented finite diagram.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf; expanded normalized adjunction/Yoneda argument (Categories Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Let $(T,p_j:T\to V_j)$ be a limit cone of a finite diagram. The cone $(h_T,h_{p_j})$ is a limit of sheaves: for any sheaf $A$ and compatible maps $s_j:A\to h_{V_j}$, their values at $x\in A(W)$ are a compatible family of arrows $W\to V_j$, hence give a unique arrow $W\to T$. These assignments are natural in $W$ by uniqueness, giving the unique map $A\to h_T$. The same argument applies in $\mathcal D$. Since $u$ preserves finite limits, $(uT,u(p_j))$ is a limit cone; since $L$ preserves finite limits by the cited node, so is $(Lh_T,L(h_{p_j}))$. Step 3 says $c_{V_j}\circ L(h_{p_j})=h_{u(p_j)}\circ c_T$. Consequently $c_T$ is exactly the comparison of these cones determined by their legs, by uniqueness in the limit universal property. Equivalently, composing the canonical limit comparison for $L$ with the map induced by the $c_{V_j}$ equals the comparison through $c_T$ and $h_{uT}$. This also covers the empty diagram: both cones are terminal, so their comparison is the unique terminal isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf; expanded normalized adjunction/Yoneda argument (Categories Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Write $m:G\times G\to G$, $e:1\to G$, and $i:G\to G$ for the group operations. Under the product identifications of Step 4, the multiplication on $Lh_G$ is $L(h_m)$ preceded by $(Lh_G\times Lh_G)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_{G\times G}$, and on $h_{uG}$ it is $h_{u(m)}$ preceded by $(h_{uG}\times h_{uG})\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{u(G\times G)}$. Step 4 identifies $c_{G\times G}$ with $c_G\times c_G$ under these comparisons; Step 3 for $m$ therefore says $c_G$ respects multiplication. Step 3 for $e$ and $i$, with the terminal comparison of Step 4, gives preservation of the unit and inverse. The group identities hold because they are equalities of composites of operations, diagonals and projections, which the functors and these product comparisons preserve. As $c_G$ is invertible, its inverse also respects these operations, by composing the same equations with its inverse. Finally for a homomorphism $b:G\to H$, Step 3 gives $c_H\circ L(h_b)=h_{u(b)}\circ c_G$, which is the claimed compatibility with all represented group homomorphisms.
